question: Build a debounce function from scratch
shortAnswer: Return a wrapper that clears any pending timer and schedules a fresh one on every call, so the wrapped function only runs once the calls stop for the delay period. Keep the timer id in a closure. Mention that you would also add a cancel method and preserve this and the arguments.
memoryHook: Clear the old timer, set a new one. The timer id lives in the closure, not in a variable outside.

question: Build a throttle function from scratch
shortAnswer: Track the timestamp of the last call and ignore any call that arrives before the interval has elapsed. Add a trailing call with a timer so the final event is not dropped, which is what a naive timestamp-only version gets wrong.
memoryHook: Debounce waits for silence; throttle enforces a speed limit. Remember the trailing call — the naive version loses the last event.

question: Build a typeahead / autocomplete component
shortAnswer: Debounce the query, cancel in-flight requests with an AbortController, cache results by query string, and render an accessible listbox with full keyboard support. State the four concerns up front — debounce, cancellation, caching, keyboard and ARIA — because most candidates only do the first.
memoryHook: Four concerns: debounce, cancel, cache, keyboard. Most candidates only build the first one.

question: Build an infinite scroll list
shortAnswer: Use an IntersectionObserver on a sentinel element at the bottom of the list rather than a scroll handler, because it fires off the main thread and needs no throttling. Guard against loading the same page twice, and stop observing when there are no more pages.
memoryHook: A sentinel div plus IntersectionObserver. No scroll listener, no throttling, no scroll-position maths.

question: Build a useFetch hook with loading, error and cancellation
shortAnswer: Hold status, data and error in one state object so they can never contradict each other, abort in the effect cleanup so a stale response cannot overwrite a fresh one, and remember that fetch does not reject on a 404 or 500 so you must check response.ok yourself.
memoryHook: One state object, AbortController in cleanup, and check response.ok — fetch does not throw on HTTP errors.

question: Build a virtualised list from scratch
shortAnswer: Compute which rows are visible from scrollTop divided by row height, render only those plus a small overscan buffer, and use a spacer element of the full height so the scrollbar behaves normally. Position the visible rows absolutely, or offset them with a transform.
memoryHook: One tall spacer for the scrollbar, absolutely positioned rows for the window. startIndex = scrollTop / rowHeight.

question: Build an accessible modal with a focus trap
shortAnswer: Portal it to the body, move focus in on open and restore it to the trigger on close, trap Tab within the dialog by wrapping from last to first, close on Escape, lock body scroll, and mark it with role dialog and aria-modal. The focus trap is the part most candidates skip.
memoryHook: Portal, trap, restore, Escape, scroll-lock. The trap is what people forget — Tab must not escape behind the overlay.

question: Build a star rating component
shortAnswer: Render a radio group under the hood so keyboard and screen reader support comes for free, track a hover value separately from the selected value so the preview does not overwrite the real state, and fall back to the selected value when the pointer leaves.
memoryHook: Two pieces of state: selected and hovered. Display hovered ?? selected. Radio inputs give you accessibility free.

question: Build a carousel / image slider
shortAnswer: Keep the current index in state, translate a flex track by negative index times one hundred percent, and wrap the index with modulo for looping. Pause autoplay on hover and focus, respect prefers-reduced-motion, and announce slide changes with an aria-live region.
memoryHook: One index, translateX of -index * 100%. Autoplay must pause on hover AND focus, or keyboard users can never read it.

question: Build a drag-and-drop reorderable list
shortAnswer: Use HTML5 drag events for a simple list: store the dragged index, and on dragOver of another item splice the array to move it. State that for anything production-grade you would use dnd-kit, because touch support, keyboard reordering and screen reader announcements are where hand-rolled solutions fail.
memoryHook: HTML5 drag events do not work on touch devices. That single fact is why dnd-kit exists.

question: Build a multi-step form wizard
shortAnswer: Hold all the data in one object at the wizard level and keep a step index, validating only the current step's fields before advancing. Keep every step mounted or persist values on unmount so going back does not lose input, and put the step in the URL so refresh and the back button work.
memoryHook: One data object at the top, a step index, per-step validation. Step in the URL, or the back button breaks.

question: Build a data table with sorting, filtering and pagination
shortAnswer: Keep sort, filter and page in one state object and derive the visible rows during render rather than storing them, applying filter then sort then slice in that order. Reset to page one whenever the filter changes, and put the whole view state in the URL so it is shareable.
memoryHook: Filter, then sort, then slice — in that order. Never store the derived rows; recompute them.

question: Build a toast / notification system
shortAnswer: Keep an array of toasts in a context provider, expose an addToast function that assigns an id and sets a removal timer, and render the list through a portal into an aria-live region. The key details are pausing the dismiss timer on hover and using polite versus assertive correctly.
memoryHook: Context holds the array, portal renders it, aria-live announces it. Pause the timer on hover or users cannot read long messages.

question: Build a tabs component with keyboard navigation
shortAnswer: Track the active tab id, render tablist, tab and tabpanel roles, and wire arrow keys with roving tabindex so only the active tab is in the tab order. The pattern is that Tab moves you into the tablist and arrow keys move between tabs — not Tab through all of them.
memoryHook: Roving tabindex: only the active tab has tabIndex 0. Tab enters the group, arrows move within it.

question: Implement a custom useLocalStorage hook that syncs across tabs
shortAnswer: Read lazily in the useState initialiser, write in an effect, and listen for the storage event to pick up changes from other tabs. The catch is that the storage event does not fire in the tab that made the change, so you also need to notify listeners in the current tab yourself.
memoryHook: The storage event fires in OTHER tabs, never the one that wrote. Same-tab sync needs your own event.

question: Implement a promise-based retry with exponential backoff
shortAnswer: Loop up to a maximum number of attempts, awaiting the function and returning on success, and on failure wait a delay that doubles each round before trying again. Add jitter so many clients do not retry in lockstep, and do not retry 4xx errors because they will fail identically every time.
memoryHook: Double the delay each attempt, add random jitter. Never retry a 4xx — the request itself is wrong.

question: Implement a deep clone function
shortAnswer: Recurse through objects and arrays creating new containers, and keep a WeakMap of already-cloned references so circular structures do not cause infinite recursion. Mention structuredClone as the built-in that handles most of this, and that JSON parse of stringify silently destroys dates, undefined, functions and Maps.
memoryHook: JSON round-trip kills Dates, undefined and Maps, and explodes on cycles. WeakMap handles the cycles.

question: Implement Promise.all from scratch
shortAnswer: Return a new promise, iterate the inputs, and resolve each one recording its result by index so order is preserved regardless of completion order. Count settled promises and resolve when the count reaches the input length, rejecting immediately on the first failure. Handle the empty array by resolving straight away.
memoryHook: Store by index, count completions. Order comes from the index, not from who finishes first.

question: Implement a memoize function with a custom cache key
shortAnswer: Wrap the function in a closure holding a Map, build a key from the arguments, and return the cached value when it exists. The two things to raise are that JSON stringify as a key breaks on functions and key order, and that an unbounded cache is a memory leak, so add an LRU eviction policy.
memoryHook: A Map in a closure. Unbounded cache equals memory leak — cap it with LRU.

question: Build a countdown timer / stopwatch component
shortAnswer: Do not accumulate by adding the interval each tick, because setInterval drifts. Store the target or start timestamp and compute the elapsed time from Date.now on every tick, so the display stays accurate even if the tab is throttled or the interval fires late.
memoryHook: Never count ticks — compute from timestamps. setInterval drifts, and background tabs throttle it to once a minute.

question: Build a nested comments / tree renderer
shortAnswer: Render recursively with a component that renders itself for each child, passing a depth prop for indentation. If the data arrives flat with parentId, build a lookup map first in one pass rather than filtering the array at every level, which would be quadratic.
memoryHook: The component renders itself. Flat data becomes a tree with one pass through a Map — never filter inside the recursion.

question: Implement event delegation and a simple pub/sub event emitter
shortAnswer: Event delegation attaches one listener to a common ancestor and uses event target closest to identify which child was clicked, which is how React handles all its events. A pub/sub emitter keeps a Map of event names to sets of callbacks, with on returning an unsubscribe function.
memoryHook: Delegation: one listener at the top, closest() finds the child. Emitter: Map of name to Set, on() returns unsubscribe.

question: Build a theme switcher with dark mode and no flash
shortAnswer: Store the choice in localStorage, apply it as a class or data attribute on the html element, and default to the system preference via prefers-color-scheme. The critical detail is a small blocking script in the head that sets the attribute before React renders, otherwise the page flashes light before switching.
memoryHook: A blocking inline script in head sets the class before paint. Without it you get the flash of wrong theme.

question: Build a search with filters that syncs to the URL
shortAnswer: Treat the URL as the single source of truth, reading filters from useSearchParams and writing back on change rather than mirroring them into component state. Debounce only the text input, use replace rather than push while typing so the back button is not flooded, and reset the page whenever a filter changes.
memoryHook: The URL is the state, not a copy of it. Replace while typing, push on filter change — or the back button becomes useless.
